stage: GLB Persistence Fix + Full Chain Re-Verification

glb_persistence_bug.detail: The 212-byte skeleton GLB (reported Aug 3) was resolved by prior work: _set_workflow_state no longer calls db.expire_all(), scene3d endpoint no longer filters geometry jobs by state, and geometry_result is persisted via flag_modified + flush. Fresh pipeline run produces a 10,264-byte valid GLB with 14 meshes.

glb_normals_bug.root_cause: export_glb always declared a NORMAL attribute in each primitive, but wrote a normals accessor with count=0 when mesh.normals was empty. Blender rejects NORMAL accessors whose count (0) != POSITION count (N).
glb_normals_bug.error_signature: IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0 (Blender glTF importer, do_primitives)
glb_normals_bug.fix: Added _compute_flat_normals(vertices, indices) that generates per-vertex normals (flat shading) when normals are missing or undersized. NORMAL accessor count now always matches POSITION count.

glb_chunk_length_bug.root_cause: JSON and BIN chunk headers declared UNPADDED lengths (len(json_bytes), len(bin_buffer)) while PADDED chunks were written. This corrupted the BIN chunk offset, causing Blender to read a None buffer.
glb_chunk_length_bug.fix: Chunk headers now declare PADDED lengths (len(json_chunk), len(bin_chunk)). JSON padding uses spaces (0x20) via new _pad_json_to_4 helper; buffer.byteLength stays UNPADDED per glTF spec.

validate_glb_enhancement.detail: validate_glb now does structural validation: parses JSON chunk, checks mesh presence, POSITION accessor count > 0, and NORMAL count == POSITION count. Previously it only checked magic + version, returning valid=True for GLBs Blender rejects.

verification.unit_test: export_glb with empty-normals mesh → NORMAL count == POSITION count, validate_glb passes
verification.blender_import: fixed_api_glb.glb (14 meshes, 112 vertices, 168 polygons) imports into Blender 5.2.0 cleanly — floor_slab + 13 furniture/wall components
verification.tests: 167/167 pass (suite grew from 131 to 167 since Aug 3)
